title: Affine component annihilation for the kernel
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, I and K quasi-coherent ideal sheaves, F and G coherent formal modules for I, and alpha:F→G. Fix a single affine open V and t≥1. If K(V)^t annihilates both the kernel and cokernel of the map of section limits over V, then K(V)^(2t) annihilates the sections over V of the kernel of alpha_n, for each n. No covering hypothesis is used.

source.place: Remark 0888, reduction modulo powers of I and affine kernel comparison

proof.text: The canonical projections from the two section limits to level n are surjective, with kernels J times the respective module, where J=I(V)^(n+1). Naturality of limit projections gives a commuting square with alpha_n(V).

For f,g in K(V)^t, apply the existing scalar-composite lemma to the limit map a to obtain a linear map k with k a = fg id. Lift a section x of the component kernel through the source projection to z. Its image a(z) lies in J times the target limit. Since k is linear, fg z lies in J times the source limit and projects to zero. Injectivity of the kernel inclusion on sections gives fg x=0. Ideal multiplication extends this to K(V)^(2t).

lean.statement:
theorem coherentFormalModule_kernel_component_affine_annihilation
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (I K : X.IdealSheafData) (F G : CoherentFormalModule X I) (α : F ⟶ G)
    (V : X.affineOpens) (t : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t)
    (h :
      K.ideal V ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, V.1) (LinearMap.ker
        (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight α.hom
          (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op V.1)))).hom) ∧
      K.ideal V ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, V.1)
        (↥(limit (G.obj ⋙
          SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op V.1)) :
          ModuleCat Γ(X, V.1)) ⧸ LinearMap.range
          (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight α.hom
          (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op V.1)))).hom))
    (n : ℕ) :
    K.ideal V ^ (2 * t) ≤
      Module.annihilator Γ(X, V.1)
        Γ(kernel (α.hom.app (op n)), V.1)
